description: We are Aphelion Flux Overdrive, a team passionate about space, science, and technology. After participating in 2025, we return with new ideas, experience, and the drive to build original solutions. Our skills include programming, data analysis and visualization, research, astronomy, and creative problem-solving. We welcome curious, motivated people who want to collaborate, learn, and build something meaningful together.
summary: FLARELET is a web application developed for the “Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots” challenge. We use NASA FIRMS fire detections dating back to 2000, initially from MODIS and, since 2012, also from VIIRS, and convert them into a common unit so they can be compared from one year to another. Based on this, we have created a fire calendar for Colombia, Brazil, Mexico, Australia, and the United States: users can select an area and see whether the last month is above normal, when its fire season begins and ends, and how likely a high-activity month is over the next three months, using a forecast that also incorporates NOAA climate data. To verify its usefulness in a local case, we tested it in Aipe, Huila, one of the municipalities with the highest number of fires this year. We also designed a solar-powered field kit that monitors smoke using a camera, and a game, Rancho Guardián, to teach fire prevention. This matters because, without harmonization, the sensor change in 2012 appears to show an increase in fires that never actually occurred, and anyone deciding where to monitor needs a record they can trust.
details:
FLARELET uses more than 25 years of NASA fire detections, from MODIS since 2000 and VIIRS since 2012, and converts them into a single fire activity calendar that does not change scale when the sensor changes. Based on this calendar, it identifies months with unusual activity and forecasts the following three months.

FLARELET offers a set of features focused on monitoring and understanding wildfires. The main feature is the active fire map, which displays NASA FIRMS detections by area and date range, whether for a single day, a week, a month, a year, or custom dates. These detections are color-coded according to their intensity (FRP). The area can be selected from predefined regions, by searching for a location, entering coordinates, drawing a rectangle or polygon, or using the user's location. As a complementary feature, the fire calendar displays the daily activity throughout the year and a monthly matrix dating back to 2000, allowing users to compare a selected day with what is typical for that date.

To interpret this activity, the platform includes several analysis tools. The last 30 days status works like a traffic light, indicating whether activity is low, normal, elevated, or extreme, along with its percentile compared to the 2001–2025 period. The fire season section explains when the season usually begins, when it reaches its peak, and when it ends in each area, as well as how each year performed. The harmonization analysis brings the MODIS, VIIRS, and harmonized data series together in a single graph, showing each month's anomalies and providing the option to download them in CSV format.

Looking ahead, the one-, two-, and three-month forecast calculates the probability of a month having above-normal activity and provides a risk map using 0.5° grid cells. On the homepage, a globe displays the fires detected by FIRMS worldwide during the last 24 hours.

Access to these features depends on the user's profile. Users without an account can freely explore the platform. Users with a kit can save their area, link their device, and receive alerts. Emergency services, in turn, can view active fires, extreme-risk areas, and the priorities within their region. In this case, the organization registers through its account, and an administrator must approve it.

The Flarelet Kit, which is still in the prototype phase, is the field node that can be linked by scanning its QR code. The demo account displays simulated readings, clearly marked as such, and includes a 3D viewer that allows users to explore the kit piece by piece.

Finally, the platform is offered as an installable web application for iPhone, Android, and computers. It features an iPhone-style Liquid Glass interface, light and dark themes, Spanish and English language options, and accessibility settings for large text, low vision, color blindness, and reduced motion. In addition, it includes the Rancho Guardián game, a 2D farming experience set on a floating island. Players plant crops, raise animals, and sell their products while learning to remove dry vegetation, avoid leaving controlled burns unattended, and use firebreaks. The game begins with a guided tutorial and can receive real regional risk data from Flarelet.
